## importing necessary libraries  
```{python}
!pip install palmerpenguins
```
```{python}
from palmerpenguins import load_penguins
import pandas as pd
penguins = load_penguins()
penguins.head()
```

## Cleaning penguins data

```{python}
df = penguins.dropna()
display(df.head())
df.info()
```

## Creating dummies for categorical variables
```{python}
categorical_cols = ['species', 'island', 'sex']
df_encoded = pd.get_dummies(df, columns=categorical_cols, drop_first=True)
display(df_encoded.head())
```

## Defining the models used
```{python}
target = df_encoded['bill_depth_mm']
all_predictors = [col for col in df_encoded.columns if col != 'bill_depth_mm']

predictors_model1 = ['bill_length_mm']
predictors_model2 = ['bill_length_mm', 'flipper_length_mm']
predictors_model3 = ['bill_length_mm', 'flipper_length_mm', 'body_mass_g']
predictors_model4 = all_predictors
```

## SPlitting the data into training and test data
```{python}
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split

X_train_model1, X_test_model1, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(df_encoded[predictors_model1], target, test_size=0.2, random_state=42)
X_train_model2, X_test_model2, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(df_encoded[predictors_model2], target, test_size=0.2, random_state=42)
X_train_model3, X_test_model3, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(df_encoded[predictors_model3], target, test_size=0.2, random_state=42)
X_train_model4, X_test_model4, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(df_encoded[predictors_model4], target, test_size=0.2, random_state=42)

print("Data splitting complete.")
```

## Fitting all the models and storing the predictions in the dataframe
```{python}
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
from sklearn.metrics import r2_score

results = {}

# Model 1
model1 = LinearRegression()
model1.fit(X_train_model1, y_train)
y_train_pred_model1 = model1.predict(X_train_model1)
y_test_pred_model1 = model1.predict(X_test_model1)
results['Model1 Training R-squared'] = r2_score(y_train, y_train_pred_model1)
results['Model1 Testing R-squared'] = r2_score(y_test, y_test_pred_model1)

# Model 2
model2 = LinearRegression()
model2.fit(X_train_model2, y_train)
y_train_pred_model2 = model2.predict(X_train_model2)
y_test_pred_model2 = model2.predict(X_test_model2)
results['Model2 Training R-squared'] = r2_score(y_train, y_train_pred_model2)
results['Model2 Testing R-squared'] = r2_score(y_test, y_test_pred_model2)

# Model 3
model3 = LinearRegression()
model3.fit(X_train_model3, y_train)
y_train_pred_model3 = model3.predict(X_train_model3)
y_test_pred_model3 = model3.predict(X_test_model3)
results['Model3 Training R-squared'] = r2_score(y_train, y_train_pred_model3)
results['Model3 Testing R-squared'] = r2_score(y_test, y_test_pred_model3)

# Model 4
model4 = LinearRegression()
model4.fit(X_train_model4, y_train)
y_train_pred_model4 = model4.predict(X_train_model4)
y_test_pred_model4 = model4.predict(X_test_model4)
results['Model4 Training R-squared'] = r2_score(y_train, y_train_pred_model4)
results['Model4 Testing R-squared'] = r2_score(y_test, y_test_pred_model4)

print(results)
```

## Plotting

```{python}
from plotnine import *
```


```{python}

model_names = ['Model 1', 'Model 2', 'Model 3', 'Model 4']
training_r2 = [results['Model1 Training R-squared'], results['Model2 Training R-squared'], results['Model3 Training R-squared'], results['Model4 Training R-squared']]
testing_r2 = [results['Model1 Testing R-squared'], results['Model3 Testing R-squared'], results['Model3 Testing R-squared'], results['Model4 Testing R-squared']]

# Create a pandas DataFrame for plotnine
plot_data = pd.DataFrame({
    'Model': model_names * 2,
    'R_squared': training_r2 + testing_r2,
    'Type': ['Training'] * len(model_names) + ['Testing'] * len(model_names)
})

# Create the plot using plotnine
plot = (ggplot(plot_data, aes(x='Model', y='R_squared', fill='Type'))
        + geom_bar(stat='identity', position='dodge')
        + labs(y='R-squared', title='Training and Testing R-squared for Different Models')
        + theme_minimal()
       )

plot
```

## Analysis

Based on the analysis through different models, model 1 (on bill_length as explanatory variable) performed poorly with a negative testing R-squared (-0.046). Models 2 and 3 showed moderate performance with testing R-squared values around 0.23.Model 4, using all available predictors (including one-hot encoded categorical features), achieved the highest testing R-squared (0.759), indicating it explains a substantial amount of the variance in the target variable.

The plot also shows that Model 4 had significantly higher training and testing R-squared scores compared to the other models.
